plan.planning_summary: Refining the 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack from route_01. Three complementary routes: (1) adjacency-smoothed gradient optimization with 40% reduced step size initialized from iteration_16 best candidate, (2) extended 28-layer stack to utilize more of the 30-layer budget, (3) bimodal reinitialization with thickness grouping to reduce fabrication sensitivity. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_01' per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: Adjacency-Smoothed 24-Layer Refinement with Reduced Step Size
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Applying an adjacency-smoothing penalty to discourage abrupt thickness jumps between consecutive high-index layers will improve robustness while maintaining or improving the target score, as the current best design shows thickness dispersion that may be fabrication-sensitive.
routes.design_principle: Regularize the thickness profile by penalizing large differences between adjacent HfO2 layer thicknesses, encouraging gradual gradients rather than discontinuous jumps. This follows the feedback directive to probe whether smoother periodic approximations can extract remaining performance without fabrication-sensitive discontinuities.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) × 12 | Fused Silica substrate - exactly 24 finite layers with alternating HfO2/SiO2 sequence, HfO2 first
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Minimize thickness gradient between adjacent HfO2 layers
manufacturing_considerations: Smoothing penalty reduces sensitivity to deposition thickness errors
Outermost layer is SiO2 for environmental durability per evidence
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Gradient regularization reduces fabrication sensitivity in non-quarter-wave designs
expected_advantages: Improved robustness score through smoother thickness profile
Maintained or improved target score from iteration_16 baseline of 0.842
Reduced risk of fabrication errors causing spectral degradation
known_risks: Smoothing constraint may limit achievable target score if optimal design requires thickness discontinuities
May converge to local optimum if step size reduction is too aggressive
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Initialize thicknesses from iteration_16 best candidate: [113.65, 61.50, 156.31, 62.55, 170.70, 58.41, 119.61, 64.73, 137.92, 56.84, 163.13, 65.05, 127.37, 60.87, 190.57, 63.37, 158.79, 62.54, 189.79, 64.87, 125.60, 68.59, 144.52, 46.09] nm. Apply gradient_thickness optimizer with 40% reduced step size relative to baseline. Add adjacency-smoothing penalty term that penalizes |thickness_H[i] - thickness_H[i+2]| for consecutive HfO2 layers. Evaluate over 300-1700 nm wavelength range with coherent smatrix solver. Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm and mean reflectance in 300-450 nm simultaneously. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Following feedback directive: apply 40% reduction in optimizer step size and introduce adjacency-smoothing penalty to regularize high-index layer dispersion. Initialized within ±15 nm of iteration_16 best candidate to probe smoother periodic approximations.

routes.title: Extended 28-Layer Stack Utilizing Full Layer Budget
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 24 to 28 layers (still within 30-layer limit) will provide additional degrees of freedom to improve the dichroic separation between UV reflection and SWIR transmission bands.
routes.design_principle: Use the remaining layer budget (30-24=6 layers available) to add 2 additional HfO2/SiO2 pairs. More layers in a quarter-wave or near-quarter-wave stack generally increase reflectance in the stopband while maintaining passband transmission if properly optimized.

soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: More layers increase deposition time and cumulative thickness error risk
Outermost layer is SiO2 for environmental durability per evidence
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack reflectivity increases with layer pair count per DBR theory
Evidence shows 38-layer and 79-layer stacks fabricated for high-reflectance applications
expected_advantages: Higher UV reflectance due to more reflector pairs
Potentially sharper band edge between reflection and transmission bands
More design freedom to optimize both bands simultaneously
known_risks: Increased total thickness may cause stress or adhesion issues
More layers increase cumulative deposition error
May not improve target score if 24 layers already near optimal for this material pair
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Initialize thicknesses using quarter-wave values at band center wavelengths: HfO2 layers at 100-150 nm, SiO2 layers at 80-120 nm as starting bounds. Apply gradient_thickness optimizer with standard step size. Evaluate over 300-1700 nm wavelength range with coherent smatrix solver. Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm and mean reflectance in 300-450 nm simultaneously. Ensure outermost layer is SiO2 for environmental durability. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Exploring whether additional layers (28 vs 24) can improve the dichroic performance by utilizing more of the 30-layer budget. This is a complementary approach to the smoothing refinement, testing if layer count rather than thickness profile is the limiting factor.

routes.title: Bimodal Thickness Grouping for Fabrication Robustness
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Grouping HfO2 layer thicknesses into bimodal clusters (thin vs thick) rather than allowing continuous variation will reduce fabrication complexity while maintaining optical performance, as the iteration_16 best candidate shows thickness values that cluster around distinct ranges.
routes.design_principle: Constrain HfO2 layer thicknesses to two discrete ranges (e.g., 60-70 nm and 150-190 nm based on iteration_16 candidate) to simplify deposition monitoring while SiO2 layers remain continuously optimized. This reduces the number of distinct thickness values the deposition system must achieve.

routes.revision_reason: Exploring fabrication-robust design by constraining HfO2 thicknesses to bimodal groups observed in iteration_16 results.
